chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: The Elegante lounge in Brooklyn with Shorty Allen
summary: After the show No Time for Squares he stayed nearly two years in the lounge with pianist Shorty Allen at the Elegante.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So when was the first time that you did one of these? Or had you been doing some of these to fill in all along?

Well, I was..oh I was at the Elegante..oh I forgot about that, that's in Ocean Park between Avenue J and K and I was there in the lounge.* And this was the type of place where they would bring people in like Della Reese and Johnny Mathis and try 'em out and then they'd send 'em to the Copa. That was the type of thing. But I was in the lounge with Shorty Allen, who wrote "The Rock and Roll Waltz", yeah. And Shorty Allen was a nice person. And I staid there. Maurice Mark played there sometimes, then sometimes Shorty would take off and Marty Napoleon would come in. And I staid there in that lounge for over two years..almost two years, yeah. That was in between there. After I'd left Timmy, yeah. After I'd left Austin Powell down there in Florida, you know, we were together. And then we came back to Wells' and

then after I left Wells', then... What had happened..we went in there with a show called "No Time for Squares" and it was an all colored review. Timmy was the star and we had chorus girls and what not. And so afterwards, you know, I didn't want to go right home so I'd come out and play with Shorty Allen. He had a trio and the bosses liked me and so after the engagement I just staid on there. I forgot about the Elegante, yeah.
